messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The issue described in the bug report is an infinite loop in the wrapping code of the HelpFormatter when the width is insufficient to display a word on a single line (leading to a JVM crash with OutOfMemoryError).

The failing test aims to verify that a long argument description is split correctly according to the specified width.

The key root of the problem can be found by inspecting the renderWrappedText method in the HelpFormatter class (lines 809 to 851). This method is responsible for wrapping text lines:

- The method initially finds a wrap position using findWrapPos.
- If no position is found, it appends the text and returns.
- Otherwise, it adds the line up to the wrap position, a newline, and then tries to wrap the remaining text.
- There is a while(true) loop that continues wrapping the text until it is all appended.
- Inside the loop, it sets the next line text as padding plus the remaining substring from the last wrap position.
- It again finds the wrap position in the new text.
- However, the key issue is at this condition inside the loop:
  ```
  if ( (text.length() > width) && (pos == nextLineTabStop - 1) ) 
  {
      pos = width;
  }
  ```
  This condition attempts to address the infinite loop for some cases by forcing pos to width when the wrap position is problematic.
  
Looking at the method findWrapPos (lines 866-910) which is used to find the wrap position in the text:

- It first checks for newline or tab characters within width from startPos and returns that as a wrap position if found.
- If the remaining text length is less than width, it returns -1 (no wrap needed).
- Then it tries to find the last whitespace character before startPos+width by moving backward.
- If it finds one, it returns that position.
- Otherwise, it looks for the first whitespace character after startPos+width moving forward.
- It returns the position if found, else -1.

The infinite loop described in the bug occurs when there is a word longer than the wrap width, i.e., no whitespace before or after the wrap position. This causes findWrapPos to return a position exactly at or near nextLineTabStop-1 perpetually, because no wrap is possible within the width constraints, but the code incorrectly attempts to wrap it repeatedly without progress.

This results in the while(true) loop in renderWrappedText never exiting, leading to OutOfMemoryError.

The failing test confirms this, as the width of 22 is shorter than the long option text, causing the word wrapping logic to enter this infinite loop condition.

In summary:
- The bug arises in HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText with its treatment of text wrapping for words longer than width.
- The findWrapPos logic returns positions that cause an off-by-one or no progress in substring advancement.
- The while(true) loop then iterates infinitely because the substring does not shorten.
- The test triggers this by providing a long argument description that cannot be wrapped correctly within the given width.


This diagnosis aligns fully with the symptoms and the provided code.

Next step would be to fix renderWrappedText and potentially findWrapPos to correctly handle words longer than allowed width, by ensuring progress is made and infinite loops are avoided.

The methods to fix would be: HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText and possibly HelpFormatter.findWrapPos.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).

HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText(StringBuffer, int, int, String)
HelpFormatter.findWrapPos(String, int, int)
